Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed collision in a parking lot with complaints of
lower back pain and muscle spasm. The mechanism of the impact is consistent with the
lumbar strain diagnosed, and the reported symptoms align closely with the force
involved. Over the course of 18 visits, treatment followed a conventional progression
consisting of manual therapy, targeted stretching, core strengthening, and home
exercise instruction. Range of motion and paraspinal tenderness improved steadily, and
visit frequency was reduced as function returned. Imaging and physical examination
findings clearly confirm the soft tissue injury. The patient reports a remote, minor
strain in the same region several years ago that resolved completely without lasting
limitation. Billing records reflect single enrties for each service with no repeated
charges. At discharge the patient was ambulating independently with near-normal lumbar
mobility and was advised to continue a self-directed exercise program.

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.

- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.
